Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Los Angeles/Oxnard CA 
855 PM PST Wed Nov 11 2026

.SYNOPSIS...11/459 PM.

A significant cooling trend will begin Thursday, with 
temperatures falling to near normal by Friday. Off and on rain is
expected Thursday night into early Saturday and more storms are 
possible next week.

&&

.SHORT TERM (WED-SAT)...11/134 PM.

Big cooling coming Thursday and Friday as the next storm 
approaches. Rain timing has sped up slightly with the latest 
models and we could see some light showers as early as 10pm 
Thursday night from Santa Barbara west and by 5am Friday 
everywhere else except the far interior areas. High res models 
also indicating a small chance of some lightning as this first 
impulse moves in though most of those chances are from Orange 
County south. In terms of rain rates, models are showing around a 
30-40% chance of 0.50/hr with this first impulse south of Point
Conception, but for most areas hourly rates should be under a 
quarter inch.

Showers will taper off after sunrise Friday but some isolated
light showers are possible through the day.

The next impulse will hit the Central Coast late afternoon on
Friday and advance south of Pt Conception Friday night into early
Saturday morning. Any areas that don't get wet Friday morning 
should get wet Friday night. Peak rain rates will be about the 
same so still not expecting any significant impacts. For most 
areas rain will be finished before sunrise Saturday. Rain totals 
in most areas through Saturday are expected to be between a half 
and one inch.

.LONG TERM (SUN-WED)...11/220 PM.

Sunday should be a pleasant day as a little pop up ridge moves
over the area. Highs will be in the mid 60s to lower 70s, very
close to seasonal norms.

Another storm is expected Monday, though could be as late as early
Tuesday depending whether the system tries to dig farther south
before moving inland as the latest GFS is hinting at. The EC is
more progressive. The ensembles seem to favor the earlier arrival.
Then a potential third system late Wednesday into Thursday.
Neither of them appear to be too impactful at this time, though
there are maybe 10-20 percent of the solutions showing a potential
1-3" of rain with that Thursday system.

&&

.AVIATION...12/0454Z.

At 0450Z at KLAX, the marine inversion was 600 feet. The top of
the inversion was 1400 feet with a temperature of 24 degrees
Celsius.

For the 06Z TAF package, moderate confidence in KPRB, KSBP and
KSMX as there is a 50% chance that CIG/VSBY restrictions do not
develop overnight. 

For sites south of Point Conception, high confidence in CAVU
conditions through the period.

KLAX...High confidence in 06Z TAF as CAVU conditions are expected
through the period. There is a 10% chance of IFR/LIFR conditions
10-17Z. No significant easterly wind component is expected.

KBUR...High confidence in 06Z TAF as CAVU conditions are expected
through the period.

&&

.MARINE...11/217 PM.

For the Outer Waters, moderate to high confidence in current 
forecast. Seas will remain slightly below SCA levels through 
Wednesday, except for PZZ670 where seas will hover near 10 ft. 
Expecting 10+ ft seas to return Thursday through at least early 
next week, with models indicating potential for wave heights 15 to
20+ ft this weekend - peaking on Saturday. A secondary but lower 
peak in seas is expected Monday. SCA winds are likely near and 
south of Point Conception Friday night through Saturday night, 
and for a shorter time north of Point Conception as the front 
moves through.

For the Inner Waters north of Point Sal, moderate to high 
confidence in current forecast. Conditions are expected to 
remain below SCA levels through Thursday. SCA level seas could 
return as early as late Thursday night or Friday, peaking over the
weekend. Gusty SCA level winds are possible nearshore Friday 
night through Saturday afternoon. 

For the Inner Waters south of Point Conception, moderate to high
confidence in current forecast. Winds and seas are expected to 
remain below SCA levels for the southern Inner Waters through 
Thursday. SCA winds will then be possible at times Friday night
through Saturday.

There is concern for a large westerly swell this weekend which 
could produce dangerous breaking waves at Ventura and Morro Bay 
harbor entrances.

There is a chance of showers sometime from Thursday night into 
the weekend across the coastal waters.

&&

.BEACHES...11/804 PM.

A very large, long-period west to northwest swell originating 
from a strong aleutian low pressure system will arrive at the 
beaches this weekend. Impacts will be focused along west to 
northwest facing shores and are expected to peak on Saturday. 
Significant beach erosion and shallow flooding of sea water over 
low-lying beach walkways, parking lots, and roads is likely,  
especially in the morning hours near high tide. Large surf will 
create dangerous rip currents, along with strong long shore 
currents, potential sneaker waves and large shore pound. Impacts 
will be less for south-facing shores.

The highest risk will be along the Central Coast with potential
for localized damage to the most vulnerable areas - such as
to piers, roads, and structures. A coastal flood watch has been 
issued to highlight the potential for WARNING-level inundation, 
such as widespread flooding at Oceano Dunes State Park. There
is a HIGH chance for WARNING-level Surf which current guidance
shows potential for 18-25 ft across northwest facing shores. 

For LA/VTA west-facing beaches, there is potential for at least
advisory level surf and cannot rule out a High Surf WARNING
especially for the Ventura coastline. 

Coastal hazards are likely to continue well into next week as the
northern Pacific remains very active.
